content: Hi, how can I support your content project today?
I need help drafting a promotional SMS for my small shop's Spring Sale.

Absolutely! To make your SMS effective, I recommend a structure with three parts: an attention-grabbing opening, a concise message about the sale, and a friendly call-to-action. This keeps your message clear and engaging. Would you like to share any specific details to highlight?
We're offering 20% off on all garden supplies this weekend. Can you put that into a catchy SMS?

Here's a draft for your SMS:

"Spring into savings!  Enjoy 20% off all garden supplies this weekend at [Your Shop Name]. Don't miss out, visit us and get growing!"

I started with a playful phrase to match the season, stated the offer clearly, and ended with an upbeat call-to-action. This should encourage customers to visit without sounding pushy.
That's nice! Could you make it shorter? I want to be sure it fits one message.

Of course! Here's a concise version:

"Spring Sale! 20% off garden supplies this weekend at [Your Shop Name]. See you soon!"

This keeps the core information and a friendly closing, making it suitable for a single SMS.
Perfect. Could the call-to-action be a little more specific, like inviting them to stop by?

Certainly! Here's a revised closing:

"Spring Sale! 20% off garden supplies this weekend at [Your Shop Name]. Stop by and save!"

This version directly invites customers in, making the message more inviting without any pressure.
